monthly_review.summary: You've increased training intensity significantly this month, trading volume for higher-quality efforts — reflected in faster pace, higher HR, more Z3–Z4 time, and elevated aerobic TE, though total distance dropped.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone 3 time jumped from 36% to 32% last month to 32% this month — but Zone 4 surged from 12% to 21%, indicating a strategic shift toward threshold work.

goal_tracker.message: You need 7.6 more km across 2 sessions in the remaining 13 days to match last month’s volume — e.g., two 4.0 km runs at your current avg pace (8:26 min/km) would exceed the target.

insights.title: Efficiency improved despite higher intensity
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.28 to 13.44 m/sec per bpm — meaning you’re generating more speed per heartbeat, likely due to recent threshold efforts (e.g., 4.6 TE run on 4/12 at 7:25 min/km, HR 163).

insights.title: Over-reliance on Zone 3–4, minimal recovery stimulus
insights.body: Z1 time dropped from 4% (last month) to just 10% this month — and no run this month spent >5% in Z1. Meanwhile, Z3+Z4 now accounts for 53% of time vs 48% last month, compressing recovery capacity.

insights.title: Stride length variability correlates with pace and HR stress
insights.body: Stride length ranged from 70.96 cm (6.2 km easy run, HR 142) to 90.77 cm (5.0 km hard run, HR 163); vertical oscillation stayed stable (7.8–8.4 cm), suggesting efficient form adaptation under load — but ground contact time increased slightly on slower runs (314 ms on 4/17 vs 306 ms on 4/12), hinting at fatigue or pacing inconsistency.

insights.title: Aerobic TE accumulation is accelerating, but distribution lacks balance
insights.body: Avg aerobic TE rose to 3.4 — up from 3.0 — yet only one run this month had TE <3.0 (2.8 on 4/1), and zero were ≥5.0. This suggests consistent moderate-to-hard efforts without true low-stress aerobic base work or high-intensity peaks.

recommendations.action: Do a 5.5 km Zone 2 run (HR ≤135 bpm) at 9:00–9:30 min/km on your next easy day, prioritizing Z1–Z2 time — aim for ≥15% Z1 time (per Garmin post-run breakdown).
recommendations.reason: Z1 time fell to just 10% this month (vs 4% last month, still critically low), and your easiest recent run (4/17) was at 9:08 min/km but HR 144 — too high for true recovery stimulus.

recommendations.action: Repeat your 4/12 session format (5.0 km at ~7:25 min/km, HR ~163) — but reduce distance to 4.0 km and add 2×1-min walk breaks between kilometers to keep average HR ≤160 and maintain stride efficiency (target stride length ≥88 cm).
recommendations.reason: That run delivered your highest TE (4.6) and best stride length (90.77 cm), but ground contact time dipped to 306 ms — indicating neuromuscular freshness; replicating it at lower cumulative stress preserves quality.

recommendations.action: Add a 12-min post-run mobility routine focusing on hip flexor release and calf elasticity after every run this week — especially following any run with vertical oscillation >8.2 cm (e.g., 4/3 and 4/12 both hit 8.3–8.4 cm).
recommendations.reason: Elevated vertical oscillation on harder efforts may reflect compensatory stiffness; your VO2 max rose from 34.0 to 35.0, suggesting readiness to support better economy with mobility work.

weekly_focus.description: Rebuild autonomic resilience by widening the gap between pace and HR stress — using deliberate low-HR running to reinforce aerobic infrastructure while preserving recent gains in threshold efficiency.
suggested_sessions: Zone 2 endurance run (5.5 km, HR ≤135 bpm)
Short threshold repeat (4 × 1 km @ 7:25 min/km w/ 90-sec walk rest)
Recovery run + mobility (3.5 km easy + 12-min routine)
